vulnerability.name: Deleted-binary (fileless) process
vulnerability.author: Thomas Shaw
vulnerability.description: A long-running process whose on-disk executable has been unlinked, so it survives only in memory (/proc/<pid>/exe reads "(deleted)"). It overwrites its argument vector to masquerade as a kernel worker thread ([kworker/...]) that the live tools print, while its kernel task name (comm) holds the real, build-specific name decoded into RAM at runtime. That name never appears in the on-disk binary and is recoverable from a memory image (Volatility psscan reads comm directly, past the argv disguise) or the live process. Teaches that argv can be forged but the kernel's own task name survives in a capture, and why volatile evidence must be collected before powering a system down.
vulnerability.hint: A process can keep running after its executable is deleted from disk.
vulnerability.solution: Find the process whose /proc/<pid>/exe is marked "(deleted)", then read its real name from the task's comm field (Volatility psscan on a RAM capture, or ps -o comm on the live process); the argv column shows a forged [kworker/...] name, and the real name is in no file on disk.
